advances: A fixed-normal measure comparison under explicit ball and face-equivalence assumptions. It also covers dimension-zero alignment and pushforward domination.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Equivalence to intrinsic measure gives closed support $F_i$ for each $\mu_i$, including a singleton when $m_i=0$. Fix $x\in F_A$. For every $y\in F_B$ and $\epsilon>0$, use the two balls of radius $\epsilon$ at $x,y$ and $P_r(s,t)\ge 2^{-r}t$ to get
$$
\mu_K(B(T_x(y),\epsilon))\ge 2^{-r}\mu_B(B(y,\epsilon)).
$$
Put $\nu=(T_x)_\#\mu_B$. Its mass in $B(T_x(y),\epsilon)$ equals $\mu_B(B(y,2\epsilon))$. When $m_B>0$, Lebesgue differentiation in the affine hull of $F_B$ gives a finite positive ball-density limit at $\mu_B$-almost every $y$, so the ratio $\mu_B(B(y,\epsilon))/\mu_B(B(y,2\epsilon))$ tends to $2^{-m_B}$ there. When $m_B=0$ the ratio equals one. The differentiation theorem for finite Radon measures with respect to another finite Radon measure using Euclidean balls gives $\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\mu_K(B(z,\epsilon))/\nu(B(z,\epsilon))=d(\mu_K)_{\rm ac}/d\nu(z)$ for $\nu$-almost every $z$, where the absolutely continuous part is relative to $\nu$. This proves $\mu_K\ge 2^{-(r+m_B)}\nu$.

The positive measure $\nu$ is carried by an affine space of dimension $m_B$. If $m_K>m_B$, that space is null for intrinsic $m_K$-measure on $F_K$, hence null for $\mu_K$, a contradiction. This gives $m_K\le m_B$, and symmetry gives $m_K\le m_A$. Let $L_i$ be the directions of the three affine hulls. The affine hull of the midpoint set has direction $L_A+L_B$, since endpoint differences can be taken with the other endpoint fixed. Inclusion gives $L_A+L_B\subset L_K$ and $m_K\ge\max(m_A,m_B)$. All dimensions must then coincide and the three directions must agree. Inclusion of the midpoint set in $F_K$ makes the affine hull of that set equal to $\operatorname{aff}F_K$.

Suppose $m\ge1$. Choose any endpoint origins in their affine planes, the average of those origins in the middle plane, and one orthonormal coordinate system on the common direction space. The intersections of ambient balls centered in these planes with their own planes are intrinsic balls with the same radii. The density representatives in the statement are Borel: for fixed radius the open-ball mass is Borel in its center, and the limits and upper limits can use rational radii. Indeed for any real radius the open-ball mass is the limit from increasing rational radii below it, as is the normalized mass. Intrinsic Lebesgue differentiation gives the full endpoint sets and the almost-everywhere equality for the middle density. For any $x\in E_A,y\in E_B$, the endpoint masses are positive for all sufficiently small radii. Divide the equal-radius ball inequality by $\omega_m\epsilon^m$ and use degree-one homogeneity of $P_r$ before taking the upper limit at the middle point. This gives its first lower bound. Arithmetic-geometric mean gives $P_r(s,t)\ge\sqrt{st}$ and $( (s^{-1/m}+t^{-1/m})/2)^{-m}\le\sqrt{st}$ for positive $s,t$, proving the second bound. The upper-density version allows infinite values at exceptional target points even when a particular endpoint pair has its midpoint at such a point.
statement:
Let $r\ge1$ be an integer and let $F_A,F_B,F_K$ be nonempty compact convex sets in a Euclidean space with $(F_A+F_B)/2\subset F_K$. Let $\mu_i$ be finite nonnegative measures equivalent to intrinsic Hausdorff measure on $F_i$, with $m_i=\dim\operatorname{aff}F_i$, for $i=A,B,K$. Suppose for every pair of open balls $B(x,a),B(y,b)$ with positive corresponding endpoint masses,
$$
\mu_K\bigl(B((x+y)/2,(a+b)/2)\bigr)
\ \ge\
P_r\bigl(\mu_A(B(x,a)),\mu_B(B(y,b))\bigr),
\qquad
P_r(s,t)=\left[\frac{s^{1/r}+t^{1/r}}2\right]^r.
$$
Then for every $x\in F_A$ the map $T_x(y)=(x+y)/2$ satisfies $\mu_K\ge 2^{-(r+m_B)}(T_x)_\#\mu_B$, with the symmetric statement interchanging $A$ and $B$. The three affine hulls have equal dimension $m$ and one common direction space, and their averaged endpoint affine hull is $\operatorname{aff} F_K$.

If $m\ge1$, write $\omega_m$ for the unit $m$-ball volume and let $E_i\subset F_i$ be the full $\mu_i$-measure Borel set where the intrinsic ball-density limit $f_i(x)=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\mu_i(B(x,\epsilon))/(\omega_m\epsilon^m)$ is finite and positive, for $i=A,B$. The Borel upper density $g^+(z)=\limsup_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\mu_K(B(z,\epsilon))/(\omega_m\epsilon^m)$ on $\operatorname{aff}F_K$ agrees with the density of $\mu_K$ almost everywhere for intrinsic Lebesgue measure. For every $x\in E_A$, $y\in E_B$,
$$
 g^+((x+y)/2)\ \ge\ P_r(f_A(x),f_B(y))
 \ \ge\ \left[\frac{f_A(x)^{-1/m}+f_B(y)^{-1/m}}2\right]^{-m}.
$$
title: Alignment and pointwise density bounds for conditional surface faces
